column3: That the Rosario marriage index showed "Larena V x Sarmiento A" at Libro 9 folio 20 - and that this was a candidate
column4: The entry reads *** LAVENA V. x BELMONTE A. ***. It was misread at low resolution and kept a false candidate alive for two days.
column5: Read again at the film's maximum resolution on 10 September. Not close: the hand is unambiguous.

column3: That a cluster of Larena/Lerena at Cayasta might be a kindred
column4: Cayasta is an ITALIAN colony - Laurini five times, Lauron, Castelarin - and the same mother is transcribed Azela in one act and Raiela in another. The "cluster" was a transcription artefact.
column5: Reading the acts instead of the index. Retracted publicly; the register entry is now EXCLUDED.

column3: That the 1869 census showed a Llerena HOUSEHOLD at Rosario
column4: The image shows twelve separately-numbered, unrelated individuals in a conventillo. There is ONE man of the name, Bartolome, not a family.
column5: Opening the image instead of trusting the index grouping.

column3: That Gabino L. Llerena was a Rosario-born link between the two countries
column4: Every other person on his record is Uruguayan, so the Rosario in question is Rosario, COLONIA, in Uruguay.
column5: Caught before it was published, by reading the rest of the record.

column3: That reading the Rosario registers needed the Chrome extension, because the in-app browser could not crop
column4: Wrong twice. The viewer has its own zoom, and - far more important - the Image Index panel is an HTML TABLE. The handwriting never needed to be read at all.
column5: David: "why do you need chrome? use your own browser?"

column3: That "Armand[o] Lorena", born 1882 at Rosario de Lerma, Salta, was "probably not him" - written off on four objections
column4: It IS him. The image reads "Clase de 1882 / LERENA - Pablo Armando / hijo de JUAN CARLOS LERENA y de MARIA LERENA / Nacido en Rosario de Santa Fe / Oficina enroladora de CAPETOWN". Three of the four objections were artefacts of a machine index that dropped "Pablo", moved him 1,400 km, wrote Lerena as Lorena, and invented the surname "Serena" out of the printed word SERIE.
column5: Opening the image. It took two minutes. *** This is the most serious error in the archive: the central finding of the project was nearly discarded. ***

column3: That Roque's first wife was "Rosalina Wilhelmina CHAPPELL", read from a marriage index
column4: CHAPPELL was her MARRIED name. She was Roseline Wilhelmina FORBES, widow of Frederick Christian Chappell. The 1936 register calls her "Rosaline Wilhermina Forbes Chappell" because that is what a remarrying widow is called.
column5: The 1920 Chappell-Forbes marriage, found in BOTH the civil and the Anglican registers, plus Chappell's own estate file.

column3: Margin readings taken from register openings rendered at 42% scale
column4: Not reliable. At that size "Timoteo Lucero" was read as "Armando Sara" - both words wrong, and an L-surname missed, which is the exact failure that matters when hunting one L-surname. Every opening was re-read from the margin strips at maximum resolution.
column5: Zooming on a single doubtful entry, and finding it was not doubtful at all - it was simply wrong.

column3: That the Lerena palette was identical to the FALCO archive's, with hex values quoted
column4: The values quoted were Falco's, not ours. The Lerena styles.css is byte-identical to the DEFRANCESKI archive's. Falco is the outlier, with a warm palette against the shared cool one.
column5: Reading both files side by side instead of trusting memory.

column3: That the Italian-origin hypothesis was "the most consequential thing on this page"
column4: Within the hour, the low-confidence genetic groups showed no Italian group among the five legible ones - evidence against it. Downgraded the same day to "already weaker than when it was written".

column2: The four LERINA arrivals of 1889 were excluded partly for the wrong reason
column3: The register said they were excluded because "LERINA here is an Italian surname, not a variant of the Spanish Lerena." That is a claim about the NAME, reached from an index without opening the manifest - the same move that got the Armando Lorena card wrong and had to be corrected in public. The four are still excluded, but on the dates and the composition of the party: they arrive in 1889, aged 59, 55, 21 and 17, seven years after Pablo Armando was born at Rosario, and the party contains no Juan Carlos and no Maria. The surname claim is withdrawn as a reason. Flagged by this archive's own search box, which noticed that all four LERINA entries carried the same unexamined label.

column2: Two different Arturo Lerenas were written up as one man - caught within the hour
column3: A table published this evening said the Arturo Lerena in army drawer Cajon 985 was born at Montevideo in 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel. That was a conflation. The Uruguayan record it rested on names the man's wife as EMA REGULES - and Ema Regules married JUAN ARTURO Lerena Traibel (1861-1936), whose children were born at Montevideo between 1881 and 1887. The Arturo in the drawer married AMALIA DIAZ and had children in La Pampa, Mendoza and Entre Rios between 1889 and 1897. Two men, one surname, one given name. The row is withdrawn and the "four branches" claim is now three. Caught by opening the FamilySearch Tree profile that the record was attached to, which is the same move - go to the underlying record - that this archive keeps having to learn.
